newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end higher on offshore funds' buying.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end higher on offshore funds' buying.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed higher on Friday as offshore funds bought some blue chips on bargain hunting, brokers said.
"Offshore funds seem to be betting on the belief that such stocks were oversold recently as a result of Kia's troubles," said Na Min-ho, a broker at Daishin Securities.
The composite stock index closed 7.65 points higher or 1.03 percent at 747.37.
"A handful of blue chips led today's rise. It is hard to tell whether the market will rise further tomorrow," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.
Trading volume totalled 40.98 million shares, compared with 44.02 million on Wednesday.
The market was closed on Thursday for a national holiday.
Gainers outpaced loseres 410 to 370 with 119 unchanged.
Brokers said rumours on an early expansion of the foreign stock ownership limit helped buoy overall sentiment.
Officials at the finance ministry flatly denied the speculation.
Samsung Electronics gained 1,700 won to 68,100 and KEPCO was up 1,100 won to 27,800. POSCO also closed 1,200 won higher at 64,000.
Five of Kia's six listed companies went limit-down and the banking sector remained weak from the Kia shock.
Kia Motors fell 900 won to its lower-limit of 11,500, but Asia Motors gained 80 won to 3,350.
"Investors began to buy Asia shares because the price was so cheap," said Na of Daishin.
The sub-index for bank shares fell 0.46 percent to 339.63.
Korea First Bank, a main creditor of Kia, dropped 170 won to 3,050.
SKC Ltd 43051.KS, which began trading for the first time on Friday, and two other IPO shares ended the day higher, the Korea Stock Exchange said.
Shares of SKC, storage media producer unit of the Sunkyong Group, closed at 22,600 won, up 1,600 won. Volume totalled 449,000 shares.

Young Chang Silup Co, a leather goods maker, ended 1,400 won higher at its daily upper limit of 19,900. Volume was low with 320 shares changing hands. Hankook Steel Co 60040.KS, a machinery and equipment maker, closed at 2,800 won at its limit high of 38,800. There were only buy bids.
